sections.h2: Where a Morrow County deed is recorded
sections.html:
Morrow County deeds and mortgages are recorded at the county recorder's office inside the courthouse at 48 E. High St., Mt. Gilead, OH 43338. Call 419-947-3060. The counter is open weekdays from 8 until 4. More is on the recorder's page.

Sellers in Cardington, Marengo, Edison and the townships make the same trip to Mt. Gilead. If you would rather not drive, file through an electronic recording company instead (see below).

The documents-filed list is broad. For a home sale or an inherited house, these are the entries you are most likely to need:

  • Deeds, including warranty, quit claim, survivorship and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages, along with releases, assignments, assumptions and subordinations.
  • Land contracts, leases, easements and powers of attorney.
  • Trusts, affidavits and certificates of transfer.
  • Liens of several kinds, such as mechanic's liens, notices of commencement and federal or personal tax liens.

Plats, condominium filings, annexations and zoning resolutions are on the list as well, so the same office holds the map side of the county's land records.

E-recording has been open for every document type since September 8, 2025. Four vendors can help: CSC, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm. Title companies and closing attorneys usually already hold an account with one of them, so a seller rarely needs to sign up personally.

Record searching moved to a different system in the same period. The records search page sends visitors to RecordHub, where you must create a login before you can look anything up. The account costs nothing, and the login requirement protects the records from cyberattacks.

sections.h2: What the auditor does before the recorder
sections.html:
Under section 319.20, the county auditor moves the parcel into the new owner's name and endorses the deed. Before that, the incoming owner or an agent for that owner files a statement of value as described in section 319.202, electronically or in three paper copies.

The statement carries two questions that matter to a Morrow seller. Has the property received a tax reduction for owner-occupied homes? And was the land ever enrolled in the Current Agricultural Use Valuation program? If the answer to the second is yes, the statement must note that the land can face a recoupment charge when it stops qualifying.

The Morrow County Auditor's conveyance fee page shows $4.00 per thousand for both real estate and manufactured homes. The grantor pays it, together with the 50 cent transfer fee that section 319.54(G)(2) sets for each parcel entered.

The recorder cannot set its own prices for the basic filing. Section 317.32 prescribes a base fee and an equal housing trust fund fee, and the office may add an optional preservation surcharge capped at five dollars, which the county keeps for general use. Payment is due when the paper is handed in, though electronic filers may settle afterward by electronic funds transfer or a similar method.

A long deed with several exhibits therefore costs more than a two-page one. Ask the title agent for a page count before closing so the check is the right size.

sections.h2: Transfers that owe no conveyance fee
sections.html:
The state statute names many transfers that skip the auditor's fee. The ones that come up most often in family and estate sales are these:

  • A deed that only corrects or confirms one already recorded.
  • A gift from one spouse to the other, or from a mother or father to a son or daughter.
  • A transfer among the heirs or devisees of one decedent where no money changes hands.
  • A deed into a trust whose maker kept an unlimited power to revoke it, and the deed back out.
  • Any transfer with no money or other valuable consideration that is not a gift.
  • A transfer made only to secure or release a debt.

When an exemption applies, the filing states the reason for it. If you are unsure whether a family deed qualifies, phone the auditor before the paperwork goes to the recorder.

Ohio's section 5301.01 requires the grantor to sign the deed and to acknowledge the signature before a judge or clerk of a court of record, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary public or a mayor. In practice most sellers use a notary at the title company or a bank.

If a mortgage is being paid off from the sale, the lender's release has its own clock. Under section 5301.36, the mortgagee must record the release within ninety days of satisfaction. Check the recorder's index a few weeks after closing to confirm it appears.

The recorder's office offers a free fraud alert service called Property Check. A subscriber is told when a document is filed against a named property, which helps catch a forged deed or a bogus lien early. It suits anyone whose house sits empty or came through an estate, since nobody is opening the mail there.

Alerts do not replace a periodic look at the record. A quick RecordHub search under your own name every so often costs only the time it takes to log in.

Morrow County sits in central Ohio and belongs to the Columbus metro area. The 2025 estimate is 36,305 residents living among 14,981 housing units. Owners occupy 81.2 percent of homes, and the median value is $222,300. The county is mostly owner-held, so most deeds recorded here are ordinary owner-to-owner sales.

sections.h2: What belongs in the packet before closing
sections.html:
A clean filing starts with a deed that names the grantor exactly as the prior recorded deed does. The auditor's transfer step uses a reference to the earlier recorded instrument, so a mismatch in spelling or a missing prior-deed citation can hold things up. Bring the full legal description, the grantee's mailing address and the signed statement of value.

Also confirm whether the parcel was ever in the farm-use program. An application for that program carries a one-time $25 fee and has a filing cutoff on the first Monday of March. Land removed from the program owes a recoupment charge equal to the savings of three years. A seller who sold off a few acres of a farm should ask the auditor how a split affects that charge.

Finally, ask the closing agent who will hand in the paperwork and by which route. A paper deed goes through the courthouse offices in a set order, while an e-recorded deed goes through the vendor's system. Knowing the route tells you when to expect the recorded copy.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Morrow County recorder?
faqs.a: Dial 419-947-3060. The counter is inside the courthouse at 48 E. High St. in Mt. Gilead, and its weekday hours end at four in the afternoon.

faqs.q: Does Morrow County accept deeds filed online?
faqs.a: Yes, through electronic recording vendors: CSC, Simplifile, ePN and Indecomm. E-recording has covered all documents since September 8, 2025.

faqs.q: What is the Morrow County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The county auditor charges $4.00 per thousand. The grantor pays it at the auditor's office, along with a 50 cent per parcel transfer fee set by state law.

faqs.q: Do I need an account to search Morrow County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes. The records search now runs through RecordHub, and users create a free login. The step protects the records from cyberattacks.

faqs.q: Is a deed between family members free of the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: Some are. State law exempts gifts between spouses and between a parent and child, and transfers among heirs of one decedent for no money. The filing must state the exemption, so check with the auditor first.
